# Lab 8.5: JavaScript Includes & Reusable Code

## What We Are Going to Do
Put shared constants and functions in the `includes` folder and use them to generate repeated SQL.

## Steps

1. **[Console] Create constants.** `includes/constants.js`:

<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">

const COUNTRIES = ["India", "Japan", "Brasil", "United States"];
module.exports = { START_DATE, COUNTRIES };</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


2. **[Console] Create a helper.** `includes/helpers.js`:


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • JAVASCRIPT
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">function countIf(column, values) {
  return values.map(v =&gt; `COUNTIF(${column} = '${v}') AS ${v.toLowerCase().replace(/ /g, "_")}`).join(",\n  ");
}
module.exports = { countIf };</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


3. **[Console] Use them in a model.** `definitions/marts/orders_by_status_wide.sqlx`:


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">config { type: "table" }

SELECT
  u.country,
  ${helpers.countIf("o.status", ["complete", "shipped", "returned", "cancelled"])}
FROM ${ref("stg_orders")} o
JOIN ${ref("users")} u ON o.user_id = u.id
WHERE u.country IN (${constants.COUNTRIES.map(c =&gt; `'${c}'`).join(", ")})
  AND DATE(o.created_at) &gt;= "${constants.START_DATE}"
GROUP BY u.country</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


4. **[Console] Read the compiled SQL.** Open the node in **Compiled graph**. The helper has expanded into four `COUNTIF` columns.

5. **[Console] Generate many tables with JavaScript.** `definitions/per_country.js`:


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • JAVASCRIPT
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">constants.COUNTRIES.forEach(country =&gt; {
  publish(`orders_${country.toLowerCase().replace(/ /g, "_")}`, { type: "view" })
    .query(ctx =&gt; `SELECT o.* FROM ${ctx.ref("stg_orders")} o JOIN ${ctx.ref("users")} u ON o.user_id = u.id WHERE u.country = '${country}'`);
});</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   Four views appear in the graph from one file.

## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| `includes/` | Shared constants and functions |
| Helper | Expands into repeated SQL |
| `publish()` | Creates actions from JavaScript |
| Benefit | Change once, update everywhere |
